leads.title: French Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Baseline decriminalisation of same-sex sexual activity in private in France; article states policy was retained in 1810 Code and followed in nations and French colonies that adopted the Code - foundation for legality in New Caledonia as French territory.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Citation detail visible: 'Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private' and 'retained in the Penal Code of 1810'.

leads.title: Law of 4 August 1982 equalising age of consent - repeal of article 331 (ex-article 334)
leads.documents: Equalised age of consent at 15 for same- and opposite-sex relations by repealing Vichy-era discriminatory provision that had raised it to 21 then 18 for homosexual relations.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'article 334 (moved to article 331 on 8 February 1945)' 'remained valid until 4 August 1982, when it was repealed under President François Mitterrand to equalise the age of consent at 15'.

leads.title: Same-sex marriage law of 2013 - National Assembly / Senate votes and Constitutional Council ruling of 17 May 2013
leads.documents: Legalises same-sex marriage and joint adoption; article expressly states 'Same-sex marriage is legal in all of France's overseas departments and territories' including New Caledonia.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'National Assembly approved the bill as a whole in a 329-229 vote' 'Senate approved the bill' 'On 17 May 2013, the Council ruled that the law is constitutional' 'signed 18 May 2013' 'published the next day in the Journal Officiel' 'first official same-sex ceremony took place on 29 May in Montpellier'.

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change - published in Journal Officiel 19 November 2016, effective 1 January 2017
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without sex reassignment surgery, sterilisation, psychiatrist certificates or medical diagnosis; requires court application; first-name change via registry office. Core trans legal-status source applicable in New Caledonia.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'On 6 November 2015, bill approved by Senate' '24 May 2016 National Assembly approved' '12 July 2016 National Assembly approved modified version' '12 October plenary' '17 November Constitutional Council ruled bill constitutional' 'signed 18 November 2016, published in Journal Officiel the next day, took effect 1 January 2017'.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Ended decades-long French legislative ban on legal gender change even after medical/surgical transition; established ECHR-based right to gender-marker change in France.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'French legislature then banned legal gender change for people for many decades, even if they had undergone medical and surgical transition, until a 1992 case, B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed this'.

leads.title: Article 225-1 French Penal Code as amended 18 November 2016 + Labour Code Chapter 2 (Code du travail)
leads.documents: Institutional anti-discrimination machinery: bans discrimination on sexual orientation (since 1985 law) and sexual identity/gender identity (added July 2012, wording changed to gender identity 2016) in employment, housing, goods/services.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'In 1985, national legislation was enacted' 'In July 2012, French Parliament added sexual identity' 'On 18 November 2016, new law amended article 225-1 to replace sexual identity with gender identity' plus quoted Labour Code text.

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 / 30 December 2004 creating Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité + amendment to Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881
leads.documents: Hate-crime / hate-speech enforcement machinery: criminalises homophobic, sexist, racist comments (45,000 euro fine and/or 12 months imprisonment cited), creates High Authority against Discrimination, increases penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; 2017 extension making transphobia aggravating factor for imprisonable crimes.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'On 31 December 2004, National Assembly approved amendment' 'law of December 2004 created the Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité' 'Title 3 and articles 20 and 21 amended Law on Freedom of Press of 29 July 1881' 'In 2017, transphobia became a cause of aggravation for all crimes that can be punished by prison'.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe 2022 report on gender affirming healthcare in France
leads.documents: Documents significant issues with provision of gender affirming healthcare in France: lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location; recommends informed-consent/self-determination system. Directly relevant to trans visitor healthcare expectations.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'A report published in 2022 by ILGA-Europe found significant issues with the provision of gender affirming healthcare in France, including lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, and inequitable access depending on location'.

leads.title: French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred (DILCRAH) + 2022 scientific committee controversy
leads.documents: Documents French government rights-machinery for anti-LGBT hatred and 2022 controversy over committee president's membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory opposed to youth gender transition.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'French Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred (DILCRAH)' 'In 2022, it was revealed that the president of the scientific committee... was a member of The Little Mermaid Observatory'.

leads.title: 2014 study on overseas acceptance + 2013 parliamentary vote breakdown for New Caledonia deputies
leads.documents: Documents New Caledonia-specific climate: only ~20% of overseas residents saw homosexuality as sexuality like any other vs 77% metropolitan; acceptance lower where religion/family honour prominent; first same-sex marriages in Saint Martin/French Polynesia caused demonstrations; 2 New Caledonia deputies voted for same-sex marriage; article notes LGBTQ people in New Caledonia widely accepted with large nightlife/dating scene, more notable in South Province than Kanak-majority North Province.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Citation detail visible: 'A 2014 study showed that about 20% of overseas residents saw homosexuality as a sexuality like any other, compared to 77% in metropolitan France' 'Of the 27 overseas deputies... 2 from New Caledonia... voted in favor' 'LGBTQ people in New Caledonia are widely accepted, and enjoy a large nightlife and dating scene'.
